blueprint_topic: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies — methylphenidate cardiac-safety review
stem: Before the first dose of newly prescribed methylphenidate, the nurse finds a documented cardiac arrhythmia that may not have been considered when the prescription was written. What is the safest action?

options.A: Administer the dose because methylphenidate improves cardiac conduction and lowers the likelihood of clinically important arrhythmias.
options.B: Clarify the cardiac history and prescription with the prescriber before administration so the seriousness of the arrhythmia can be assessed.
options.C: Administer the dose and monitor temperature because stimulant-related cardiac risk is not affected by heart rate, blood pressure, or rhythm history.
options.D: Permanently stop all future ADHD pharmacotherapy because any previous arrhythmia automatically contraindicates every medication used for ADHD.

rationale: Current RITALIN labeling advises avoiding methylphenidate in patients with serious cardiac disease, including serious cardiac arrhythmias, and states that CNS stimulants increase blood pressure and heart rate. A newly identified arrhythmia of uncertain severity therefore requires clarification before the first dose rather than automatic administration or a blanket permanent prohibition of all ADHD treatment. B is correct.
educational_objective: Recognize when newly identified cardiac disease or arrhythmia requires prescriber clarification before stimulant administration and distinguish that review from an unsupported universal contraindication.
source_organization: DailyMed (U.S. National Library of Medicine); Sandoz Inc.
source_version_date: Revised February 2025; current DailyMed label accessed 2026-08-26
source_locator: §5.2 Risks to Patients with Serious Cardiac Disease: avoid use with known structural cardiac abnormalities, cardiomyopathy, serious cardiac arrhythmia, coronary artery disease, or other serious cardiac disease. §5.3: stimulants increase blood pressure and heart rate; monitor blood pressure and pulse.
source_claim_supported: Methylphenidate should be avoided in serious cardiac disease including serious cardiac arrhythmia and can increase blood pressure and heart rate, supporting clarification of an uncertain arrhythmia before first administration.
blueprint_locator: Pharmacological and Parenteral Therapies: evaluate medication-order appropriateness, review contraindications and pertinent data, and administer medications safely.
candidate_reasons_resolved: Rebuilt all four options as parallel medication-safety decisions and removed isolated absolute wording.
Kept the scenario's arrhythmia severity uncertain so nursing clarification is the appropriate action rather than diagnosing a permanent contraindication.
audit_note: Independent adversarial review confirms B is the only response consistent with the labeled serious-cardiac-disease warning and nursing scope. A and C disregard the warning; D overgeneralizes one uncertain arrhythmia to all ADHD pharmacotherapy.
